projects.name: Immediate Stabilization and Recovery in Cabo Delgado Province, Mozambique
projects.description:
Since 2017 the Province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique has been facing an escalating conflict, including armed violence compounded by terrorism and connections to extremist cells in East Africa and the confluence of various economic interests in the Mozambique Channel, the occurrences of socio-economic inequalities and expectations related to the exploitation of natural resources, especially among local youth and the perception of political exclusion, and few economic opportunities, affecting in particular young people, consecutive climatic shocks, and recurrent disease outbreaks. Currently, at least  1.5 million people are in need of urgent humanitarian aid1.  It is estimated that in November 2021, over 735,000 internally displaced people were located in relocation camps or informally hosted by communities across the Provinces of Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa. 

According to the Northern Resilience and Integrated Development Program (PREDIN), by the end of September 2021, attacks resulted in the loss of life of more than 2,000 citizens and forced the displacement of more than 817,000 people.   

Violent attacks by insurgents have significantly heightened protection risks, especially for women and girls. The government of Mozambique, with the strengthening of regional and international cooperation in the field of defense, including with the arrival of troops from the Republic of Rwanda and the SADC Standby Force (SAMIM), reclaimed a number of areas which had been occupied by insurgents. Prior to the arrival of the first Foreign troops on the ground in July 2021, UNDP had initiated stabilization interventions to assist the government of Mozambique in its efforts to re-establish the presence of the State in the reclaimed areas, paving the way for reconstruction and a subsequent safe and voluntary return of IDPs to their areas of origin. UNDP is already working in the districts of Macomia, Quissanga, Mocimboa da Praia and Palma. Benefiting from decades of experience in stabilization activities elsewhere on the continent and in the world, and with an office fully established in Pemba in 2021, UNDP is well positioned to support the government in three interrelated and complementary dimensions as part of stabilization: 

OUTPUT 1: Community security is improved with a focus on Rule of Law and Access to Justice, creating the foundation for social cohesion, peace and development  

OUTPUT 2: Basic services and infrastructure are rehabilitated, functional, and accessible and the capacity of local authorities are developed to improve access to service delivery 

OUTPUT 3: Socio-economic support is provided to individuals and communities, including immediate livelihood support for affected populations 

The support provided by UNDP is aligned with PREDIN's vision to restore and consolidate peace and promote sustainable socio-economic development in the Northern Region of Mozambique, particularly with its pillars 1 (Restoration and consolidation of peace and security) and 3 (Recovery, Reconstruction and socio-economic development and resilience). 

While humanitarian support continues to be provided to populations across the province of Cabo Delgado, the stabilization interventions of UNDP are meant to increase basic state service delivery capacities in areas where security has been restored to allow for the safe return of populations. UNDP supports immediate return of State presence in conflict-affected areas through rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure and institutional capacity building for the restoration of basic services as fundamental conditions for socio-economic recovery. UNDP will ensure a conflict-sensitive, human rights-based and gender-sensitive approach through its response to build forward better, laying the foundations for peace and rule of law, as emphasized by PREDIN.  

UNDP’s stabilization engagement in Mozambique is part and parcels of the Government’s priorities in Cabo Delgado, as embodied in the reconstruction plan (PRCD), and contributing to the Northern Resilience and Integrated Development Program (PREDIN). Along those lines, the present programme is fully integrated with other components of UNDP cooperation in country, as part of its new 2022-2026 programme cycle, with particular complementarity with UNDP’s decentralization programming, as well as with its social cohesion and peacebuilding work. 

UNDP’s stabilization engagement is also grounded in two of the foundational elements of UN wide engagement on internal displacement in which UNDP is called on to a critical role: on the one hand, the 2011 decision on Durable Solutions adopted by the UN Secretary-General, and the accompanying Preliminary Framework on Ending Displacement in the Aftermath of Conflict; on the other hand, the recommendations of the report of the United Nations Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel on Internal Displacement, released in September 20212. As such, the proposed programme builds on the call for development and peace actors to predictably and coherently engage as early on as possible on solutions for displacement. Although it should not be understood as a  peacebuilding intervention, stabilization is conceived as responding to the immediate and critical step on the way to building and sustaining peace, as part of the humanitarian, development and peace engagement (HDP Nexus). UNDP will ensure it engages adequately as part of the existing humanitarian and wider coordination platforms, and will work with sister agencies on the ground.

projects.name: Artisanal Fisheries Resilient Development Project (PROPEIXE)
projects.description:
The PROPEIXE goal is “sustainably increase the incomes, nutrition and food security by addressing the main barriers to sustainable production and marketing for artisanal fisheries’’. The Project Development Objective (PDO) will be to “increase the sustainability of fishery value chain returns, by promoting responsible fisheries, community conservation and restoration of ecosystems and biodiversity, while also supporting fishery community resilience through diversification of livelihoods’’.
Target Group: The artisanal fisheries interventions will cover fishing communities along the coastline, targeting mainly households who are poor and on the fringes of the market economy, with high vulnerability due to the impact of climate change. 
The total programme outreach is estimated at approximately 90.000 beneficiaries or 40,000 households corresponding to 172,000 individuals (household members) .  Among these 90.000 persons, approximately 57,500 persons will receive a full set of project services (e.g. information, demonstration and training, access to finance), while an estimated number of 32.500 persons will be directly benefiting only from the rehabilitation of feeder roads.

It focuses on providing emergency shelter and essential household items, including context‑appropriate shelter kits, support for rapid repairs, and guidance on safer construction to enhance resilience in disaster‑prone environments. At the same time, it strengthens camp coordination and site management by improving service delivery, enhancing collaboration between stakeholders, and promoting community participation through small‑scale, community‑led improvements that reinforce ownership and accountability. The intervention also addresses water, sanitation, and hygiene needs by distributing hygiene kits, promoting key practices such as handwashing and safe water use, and improving environmental health conditions in communal spaces. In addition, it delivers protection and psychosocial support through awareness‑raising, monitoring of risks, referral services, and provision of mental health care, ensuring that vulnerable individuals receive appropriate and confidential support. Complementing these efforts, the project provides essential health services, including primary health care and disease surveillance, while strengthening the capacity of local health systems to respond effectively to emergencies. Throughout all components, the project adopts a protection‑centred, gender‑responsive, and conflict‑sensitive approach, with particular attention to the needs of vulnerable groups, ensuring inclusive and meaningful assistance for affected communities.

The overall objective of the ongoing project is to ensure dignified, safe, and secure living conditions and access to essential services for populations affected by disasters driven by natural hazards and conflict, while contributing to empowered and resilient individuals and communities across northern Mozambique. This intervention forms part of IOM’s broader multi-donor, multisectoral humanitarian response in the region, which has reached an estimated 784,319 IDPs as of February 2022.

The project is being implemented within the framework of the Humanitarian–Development–Peace Nexus (HDPN), aimed at reducing overall vulnerability, decreasing unmet needs, strengthening risk management capacities, and addressing the root causes of fragility and displacement. Through this integrated approach, the project simultaneously responds to urgent humanitarian needs while supporting recovery, resilience-building, and pathways toward durable solutions. Activities for prevention of violence and harmful practices will comprise of two inter-connected pillars: social behaviour change communication and parenting skills. Close collaboration  with social protection will ensure that vulnerable children and families do not fall through the social safety.

projects.name: Empowering displaced affected communities – scaling up the eco-system approach
projects.description: In displacement settings, internally displaced persons (IDPs) face significant challenges due to limited access to cooking fuel, lighting, electricity, and other essential energy services. This lack of energy access exacerbates hardships, increases risks of gender-based violence (GBV), puts strain on nearby host communities, and threatens local environmental ecosystems. While the humanitarian sector is beginning to prioritize sustainable energy access, data on current access levels remains scarce. Most displaced individuals in camps rely heavily on traditional biomass for cooking and have negligible or no access to electricity. IOM project aims to address these critical issues by scaling up the implementation of efficient cookstoves, integrating nature-based solutions, and expanding solar energy systems. By doing so, we seek to provide more reliable and sustainable energy sources, thereby reducing dependency on traditional biomass. This approach not only improves energy access but also allows displaced individuals greater dignity and flexibility in choosing their energy solutions.

projects.name: Strengthening community policing activities and border security systems
projects.description: Cabo Delgado in northern Mozambique has been significantly impacted by a severe context over the past seven years, driven by the Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) linked to the Islamic State. This violence resulted in the displacement of over 720 thousand people, with many fleeing to neighboring provinces and across borders into Tanzania. The insurgency has been marked by brutal attacks, including beheadings, kidnappings, and destruction of infrastructure, causing widespread fear and trauma among the local population. Allegations of human rights abuses by security forces have further eroded trust between communities and authorities, with concerns that heavy-handed responses may push more people toward supporting the insurgents. IOM’s proposed project focuses on strengthening community resilience, improving border management, and enhancing law enforcement capacity in Cabo Delgado. The project will work on three main fronts: 1) establishing community structures that link to law enforcement, creating a two-way information-sharing system; 2) building trust between law enforcement and communities through positive engagement and capacity-building; and 3) upgrading police stations and border crossing infrastructure to boost operational capacity and security. By adopting this integrated approach, the proposed project aims to contribute to effective and inclusive law enforcement services by creating a collaborative environment where safety concerns can be effectively addressed, bridging communication gaps and enhancing community engagement.

projects.name: Empowering Displaced Communities through Energy Mesh Network
projects.description: IOM Mozambique is attempting an ambitious and innovative initiative of empowering displaced communities through energy in the central provinces of Mozambique. Recognizing the critical need for sustainable energy solutions for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Mozambique, the project aims to revolutionize energy access through a groundbreaking approach. Traditional delivery models have yielded minimal impact and scale, prompting the exploration of more frugal innovations driven by the communities themselves. The project introduces a pioneering model that places the IDPs at the core of the solution development process, empowering them to actively participate in crafting and implementing sustainable energy solutions. This approach not only addresses immediate energy challenges but also ensures the longevity of impact by fostering community-led innovations. The project's focal point is to create an ecosystem where the IDPs are not passive beneficiaries but active contributors to the development and maintenance of the Energy Mesh Network. By championing a community-centric and innovative model, the project seeks to not only improve energy access but also empower displaced communities to take ownership of their energy solutions, fostering sustainability, reliability, and affordability for all.

projects.description: Mozambique is grappling with a multitude of humanitarian challenges across the country. Since 2017 the conflict has displaced over 1M people across the Northern provinces, worsening living conditions of displaced and resident communities due to the damaging/destruction of the already limited infrastructures. In addition to conflict-related displacements, cyclical extreme climate events are becoming more severe and intense, affecting communities across the country, especially in Central and Southern Provinces. International Humanitarian partners have been present in the country for decades, supporting the government and providing regular life-saving assistance to communities affected by the conflict and disasters. Recognizing the importance of localization in effectively addressing these issues and increasing the sustainability of the response and country resilience, the proposed project by IOM seeks to address humanitarian action by empowering Local and National Partners (LNAs) in Mozambique. As the first line of support for affected communities, these organizations will be allocated resources and dedicated mentoring to take ownership of interventions and lead them in accordance with the needs of their communities.

projects.name: Community stabilization for conflict-affected communities in northern Mozambique
projects.description:
For six years, the province of Cabo Delgado in northern Mozambique has experienced attacks by armed groups affiliated with the Islamic State causing over 709,529 people to be internally displaced and leaving many communities affected by loss, destruction, as well as negative economic and social impact. The insecurity in northern Mozambique is multi-faceted with many drivers including perceptions of historical marginalization and lack of economic opportunities.
This project will seek to promote community stabilization and preventing violent extremism in Northern Mozambique, particularly in communities affected by conflict with a specific focus on youth, women and girls.
In pursuit of this objective, IOM will build upon its previous work supporting community-led conflict prevention and creating a conducive environment for communities to live peaceful and productive lives through income generation activities, school-based peace clubs, community-based projects prioritized by communities and support to the Government of Mozambique to discuss mechanisms and frameworks for reintegration of former and eligible non-state armed group (NSAG) members.

projects.name: Facilitating Cross Border Mobility and Small-Scale Cross Border Trade through Implementing a Mobile Border Pass System along Mozambique/Malawi Borders
projects.description: Malawi and Mozambique are countries of origin, transit, and destination for different categories of migrants and goods. Trade, migration, and cross-border human mobility are inherently interconnected; without people, the vast majority of goods and services would be unable to cross borders and contribute to economic development. In the case of border communities, the link between people and goods becomes unavoidable in the totality of the cases. As Malawi, Mozambique, and the African Union (AU) Member States move towards the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA), the importance of effective border management policies increases as countries require measures that facilitate and expedite the movement of persons, goods, and services across borders while ensuring that important security concerns are addressed. Free Movement Protocols promulgated by the Regional Economic Communities (RECs), such as the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Protocol on the Facilitation of Movement of Persons, set out a series of measures related to a facilitated border management approach, which include visa liberalization, travel documentation, border residency arrangements among others aimed at simplifying and facilitating trade between and amongst neighbouring countries within the region and continent. In this regard, facilitating regular cross-border movement to promote trade is key for the achievement of Malawi’s and Mozambique’s development priorities. As part of efficient border management, it has a positive impact on trade, as trade agents, from small-scale traders to multinational companies, will benefit from swift, transparent, and well-organized processes at border posts (BP) and therefore, trade agents might be encouraged to increasingly use the Trade Corridors with efficient border management in place or individual men and women might be encouraged to engage in cross-border trade. This strongly contributes to increased revenues for the respective governments, creates job opportunities and contributes to economic development in general.

projects.name: IOM Mozambique Flood Response
projects.description:
The proposed interventions are aligned with the IOM Flood Flash Appeal for the response in Central and Southern Mozambique and prioritize the use of data to enable life-saving and well-coordinated humanitarian action. IOM will deploy the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) as a cross-cutting operational service to support sectoral response efforts throughout the flood emergency and early recovery phase.

DTM will provide timely, location-specific information on displacement, returns, population profiles, and priority needs across accommodation centres, host communities, and flood-affected districts. By systematically tracking mobility trends and evolving vulnerabilities, DTM will support evidence-based decision-making and allow partners to adjust interventions as conditions change, including in areas affected by residual and localized secondary flooding.

DTM data and analysis will be regularly shared with Shelter/NFI, CCCM, WASH, Health, Protection/MHPSS, and Rapid Response Mechanism partners to strengthen targeting, reduce duplication, and improve operational efficiency. This shared information base will enhance inter-sectoral coordination and support the delivery of safe, accountable, and responsive assistance to flood-affected and displaced populations.

projects.name: Provision of immediate lifesaving emergency shelter and non-food item (NFI) assistance for cyclone and flood affected populations in Central and Northern Mozambique
projects.description:
Since the first and second landfall of Tropical Cyclone Freddy, Mozambique has experienced devasting floods, destruction, and death. Damage assessments are ongoing but early reports from the National Institute of Disaster Management (INGD) show that more than 102,000 houses and homes have been damaged, destroyed, or flooded, leading to the displacement of an estimated 64,418 individuals sheltered in 164 accommodation centers across Niassa, Zambezia, Tete, Manica, Sofala and Inhambane (as of 16 March 2023). Roads and bridges have been swept away cutting off communities from much-needed support.

With the CERF RR allocation, IOM will immediately kick-start the provision of Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Item (NFI) assistance to more than 5,350 families (26,750 individuals) across the affected provinces of Zambezia, Tete, Sofala and Inhambane, in coordination with the government and partners, while also strengthening the capacities of other Shelter and NFI partners to respond to the emergency situation. The shelter interventions that will be undertaken through this allocation in Shelter sector, will include:

- Support in strengthening partner coordination and improving their capacity to respond to the immediate shelter NFI needs of an estimated 22,250 vulnerable individuals (4,450 families), by facilitating their access to, and transportation of basic shelter NFIs supplies to the mostly affected districts.

- Construction of 900 temporary emergency shelters in the relocation sites identified within Sofala and Zambezia provinces, for estimated 4,500 vulnerable individuals including consultation and technical advice on safe construction.

projects.name: A Health System Strengthing Approach to Tackling Occupational Health Challenges by Migrant Workers - Integrating Occupational and Migrant Health into National Health System (no 4)
projects.description:
Over the past seven years, IOM has developed a tailored approach to address the unique characteristics and needs of migrant mineworkers and farmer workers in Mozambique and South Africa.

IOM has partnered with the Ministry of Health (MISAU) and the Ministry of Labour (MITSS) to address the specific diagnostic and care needs of migrant mineworkers, particularly in relation to TB and HIV. This collaborative effort has involved activities such as follow-up of miners' household contacts in Mozambique and facilitating care and treatment for Mozambican miners in South Africa through cross-border referrals. Additionally, systematic screening centers have been established in Ressano Garcia on the border with South Africa since September 2018.

Since May 2020, IOM, in partnership with MISAU and collaboration with MITSS, has been implementing the project 'Tackling Occupational Health challenges faced by Mozambican miners and migrant workers'. This initiative includes comprehensive Occupational Health screening and counselling services at the Ressano Garcia Occupational Health Centre (OHC). In June 2021, two additional pre-existing OHCs in Gaza province (Xai-Xai and Mandlakazi) were integrated into the project. Through these efforts, IOM has supported the Government of Mozambique (MISAU and MITSS) and Mozambican miners in documenting occupational health conditions and accessing compensation mechanisms by providing regular and quality data on occupational diseases diagnosed in screened migrant workers.

To ensure the sustainability of advancements made in preventing and detecting occupational illnesses among migrant worker populations across southern provinces of Mozambique (Maputo, Gaza, and Inhambane) and cross-border partnerships established under the 'Tackling Occupational Health Challenges' project, IOM provided technical assistance to the Government of Mozambique in 2023 to implement a phased transition. This transition aimed to integrate the project into the national health system by ensuring continuity of service provision at OHCs, strengthening national capacity in occupational health diagnosis, streamlining data collection and reporting mechanisms, and supporting coordination of cross-border partnerships and referral mechanisms. National health system staff have been integrated in the operation of the Occupational Health Centers, and further integration is required or MISAU to take on the operation of the OHCs.

Furthermore, mobile clinics have been deployed to reach remote areas and provide essential healthcare services to migrant workers. Additionally, IOM has collaborated with the Thsiamiso Trust to ensure that migrant workers receive compensation for occupational lung diseases as part of their efforts to support access to justice and fair treatment for migrant workers.

Despite efforts including allocation and training of government human resources, the complete transition did not materialize by December 2023 as initially planned. Critical positions remain unfilled, hindering progress. Additionally, planned sourcing of essential materials and infrastructure maintenance by MISAU in Q3 2024 has not commenced.

Moving forward, IOM aims to support MISAU in developing a long-term sustainable model for providing quality occupational health services for miners and other migrant workers. This endeavor aligns with national strategies for building and strengthening Occupational Health in Mozambique.

Financial compensation from schemes like the MBOD and Tshiamiso Trust fund not only supports affected individuals but also their families, providing stability and healthcare access. With only 9 years left for the Tshiamiso Trust fund, urgent efforts are needed to locate and screen eligible beneficiaries, ensuring ill ex-miners receive rightful compensation. Additionally, families of deceased miners require attention. Through tailored health services and strengthened healthcare systems, IOM aligns with Mozambique's commitment to inclusive healthcare, as outlined in the Government's Five-Year Program (PQG) 2020-2024 and the SDG agenda.

projects.name: Saving Lives Through Anticipatory Action: Cyclone Preparedness and Response in Mozambique
projects.description:
The Shelter component will provide targeted, needs-based assistance through rapid household assessments to inform the distribution of Non-Food Items (NFIs). Beneficiary eligibility will be validated in close collaboration with local authorities and communities, with particular attention to vulnerable groups, including older persons, people with disabilities, and female-headed households. Implementation will be closely coordinated with the Shelter Cluster, which leads needs assessments, gap analysis, and pipeline stock management, to prevent duplication and ensure complementarity with other partners. Pre-positioned NFIs, such as tarpaulins and shelter repair kits, will be mobilized to high-risk districts. Accessible distribution points will be established to ensure equitable access, and distributions will be accompanied by awareness session and demonstrations on the correct use of items to maximize effectiveness and durability of assistance.  

Ahead of cyclone events, CCCM teams will work with government counterparts and the CCCM Cluster to assess, verify, and prepare priority accommodation centers and pre-position items. Support will be provided to the National Institute for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (INGD) and Local Committees for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (CLGRD) to establish safe evacuation centers, identify safe evacuation routes, and strengthen basic infrastructure to ensure protection and safety. This includes improvements to roads, drainage, sanitation facilities, pathways, and lighting, as well as the pre-positioning of essential items such as first aid kits and solar lights. 

Early warning messages from the National Institute of Meteorology will be disseminated to at-risk communities through community meetings, door-to-door outreach, and megaphone announcements led by community leaders and CLGRD members. Following cyclone impact, CCCM mobile teams will be rapidly deployed to assess site conditions and priority needs. Within 48 hours, teams will collect data on damages and displacement to inform coordination and support the government's response for internally displaced persons (IDPs), both within and outside formal accommodation centers. 

Post-impact support will include accommodation center/site management, site maintenance, rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure, debris clearance, service coordination, and community engagement. Information desks will be established to improve communication on available services and to strengthen access to complaints and feedback mechanisms and CCCM teams will facilitate access to assistance and services through coordination with district and local authorities, UN agencies, INGOs, and local organizations. Community participation will be promoted through regular consultations, operation of feedback mechanisms (including the Zite Manager platform), proactive information sharing and community-led projects.

Cross-cutting: Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA): In line with IOM's zero-tolerance policy on sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), PSEA measures will be integrated across all activities. This includes SEA risk mitigation, capacity strengthening of national and local actors, awareness-raising among affected populations on their rights to free assistance and reporting mechanisms, and referral information for survivor support services.

projects.name: Towards sustainable energy for all: Promoting market-based dissemination of integrated renewable energy systems for productive activities in rural areas
projects.description:
1. Project background information 
In Mozambique, the rural electrification rate reached only 27% as the extension of electricity grids has proven to be technically difficult, very costly and sometimes an inefficient solution due to the remoteness and sparse population density. The agricultural sector -one of the most important sectors of the economy- faces serious challenges in accessing electricity and other forms of modern energy forcing it to rely on expensive diesel, firewood and/or charcoal for its operations. Even though it has been estimated that Mozambique has a potential of 7 GW on renewable projects, the use of modern energy for productive uses is still very limited. As such, the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) –as an implementing agency of the Global Environment Facility (GEF)- and the Government of Mozambique are implementing the project “Towards sustainable energy for all in Mozambique: Promoting market-based dissemination of integrated renewable energy systems for productive activities in rural areas” which seeks –among other outcomes– to demonstrate the technical feasibility and commercial viability of renewables in productive sectors including agriculture and agro-food processing industries.

2. Project objective and description 
Through its 3 technical components, the project will support the market-based adoption of integrated renewable energy (RE) systems (solar PV for irrigation and waste-to-energy) in small to medium-scale farms and rural agro-food processing industries in Mozambique. The components are the following: 
1.	Establishment of a conducive policy and regulatory environment - the project will enhance the regulatory and policy environment to promote the involvement of the private sector in the development of integrated RE systems for rural areas. 
2.	Capacity building and knowledge management- the project will improve and develop the capabilities and knowledge of market players and enablers in the RE sector including relevant government officials (national and provincial level) as well as representatives from financial institutions, private sector, universities, and vocational training institutions. 
3.	Technology demonstration and scaling up - the project will demonstrate the technical and financial feasibility of RE technologies in agricultural activities located in rural areas, specifically: solar PV water pumping and biogas/biomass usage in agro-food processing industries through the installation of demonstration projects. The objectives of these projects, besides delivering GHG emission reductions, include generating case studies and best practices on the use of RE technologies in agro-food processing industries that have high replication potential across Mozambique. In this regard, UNIDO/GEF is offering a grant to support these demonstration projects in rural Mozambique to mitigate the high up-front costs required for such investment projects.
projects.outcome: Output 2.3 The primary sector is more sustainable, productive, value-adding and inclusive of forcibly displaced persons and incorporating circular, regenerative and gender transformative practices.

projects.name: Multi-Sectoral Response in Northern Mozambique
projects.description: The province of Nampula in northern Mozambique is confronting a convergence of climate, health, and conflict-driven crises that threaten public health, social stability, and long-term recovery and development. Recurrent cyclones have devastated critical water and sanitation infrastructure, leaving displaced and vulnerable communities reliant on contaminated sources. These conditions have precipitated persistent and severe cholera outbreaks, which disproportionately affect marginalized populations, including internally displaced persons (IDPs). The fragile health and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) systems are further strained by limited outbreak preparedness, inadequate community hygiene awareness, and weak cross-sector coordination. This vulnerability is compounded by active and escalating conflict, as evidenced by recent attacks in Memba district. According to IOM DTM Emergency Tracking reports (November 2025), these attacks have forcibly displaced over 66,000 people into Erati district, overwhelming reception sites and creating acute protection and service gaps. The potential spill-over of an ongoing Mpox outbreak from Niassa Province could further complicate the health emergency. Together, these shocks are eroding community resilience and creating conditions that heighten the risk of exploitation and recruitment by non-state armed groups (NSAGs), particularly among disenfranchised youth. The project aims to address the interconnected health, social, and economic vulnerabilities in Nampula Province, thereby promoting community stability and resilience. Through a comprehensive and context-specific intervention across the WASH and Health sectors, it will employ a joint WASH-Health approach, combining water and sanitation infrastructure rehabilitation with health system strengthening. This way, individuals will be protected and empowered to live their lives with dignity, thereby promoting greater community stability and societal resilience.

projects.name: Promoting gender-inclusive empowerment and social cohesion in displacement-affected communities in northern Mozambique
projects.description:
For over six years, northern Mozambique has faced attacks by Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) allegedly linked to the Islamic State, resulting in widespread displacement and a complex crisis with dire humanitarian implications. Among the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in the country—545,870 out of a total of 721,348—women and girls are disproportionately affected, facing heightened risks of gender-based violence, exploitation, and barriers to accessing essential services. The Northern provinces, where the majority of IDPs are located, struggle to support 55% of these individuals hosted in communities, while over 600,000 persons have returned to their places of origin, often to areas with inadequate infrastructure and limited resources.
To address this, IOM applies a Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach to this complex crisis in Northern Mozambique. Through the HDPN, IOM simultaneously responds to the direct humanitarian needs that emerged as a result of conflict and displacement and seeks to address the drivers of conflict and related displacement effects.

With this intervention, IOM will support selected displacement-affected communities by providing them with multi-sectoral assistance, enhancing their resilience and social cohesion, promoting women’s empowerment and gender equality, and facilitating their access to durable solutions in collaboration with a Japanese non-governmental organization (NGO), Peace Winds Japan, in Mocimboa da Praia.

projects.name: Strengthening Public Health Preparedness and Cross-Border Surveillance at Mozambique’s Priority Points of Entry Using a One Health Approach
projects.description:
The project “Strengthening Public Health Preparedness and Cross-Border Surveillance at Mozambique’s Priority Points of Entry Using a One Health Approach” aims to enhance Mozambique’s capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to public health threats at key border crossings, airports, and ports. Implemented by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in partnership with government institutions and health partners, the project will strengthen disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, and cross-border coordination in line with the International Health Regulations (IHR). Using a One Health approach that recognizes the interconnected health of people, animals, and the environment, the project will address emerging health risks linked to mobility, climate-related disasters, and infectious disease outbreaks.
Key activities include conducting risk assessments at priority points of entry, improving operational procedures and preparedness systems, mapping population mobility patterns to better understand disease transmission risks, and strengthening collaboration between health, immigration, border management, and local authorities.The project will directly benefit travellers, cross-border traders, transport operators, border officials, and surrounding communities, contributing to stronger health security systems, safer mobility, and more resilient border regions across Mozambique.

The overall objective of the project is to strengthen Accountability to Affected Populations in Mocimboa de Praia (MdP) district who were affected by the attacks in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique, in line with the commitment to AAP by humanitarian partners. According to mobility tracking conducted by IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), as of August 2023, 176,174 individuals had returned to MdP. In an effort to strengthen AAP and to ensure that the needs of the returnee populations are met, the project aims to improve access to key information on available services and assistance for 60,000 individuals and strengthen two-way communication channels to engage affected communities regularly. This will improve access to information for returnee populations who are facing acute humanitarian needs and enable speedy response to their needs through community feedback mechanisms established under this project. 

IOM implementing partners (IPs) will work with community-based organisations, community leadership representatives and local authorities in executing activities. The IPs will be field based and will hold regular meetings with authorities and communities to ensure that their concerns were being incorporated in the project implementation. They will recruit community mobilisers from the affected populations to strengthen the linkages with the communities. Regular meetings will hold, and joint follow up will be done with all partners utilising area-based coordination mechanisms already existing in MdP.

projects.description: Serving as a critical trade and mobility route along the border between Mozambique, Malawi and Zambia, the Nacala corridor plays a key role in the region's economic development, income growth and employment creation. The corridor serves an important trade route, including for Informal Cross-Border Trade (ICBT) which is a heavily feminized economic activity. Evidently, informal cross-border trade is important to national economies and livelihoods in the SADC region. Despite its potential for fostering economic diversification and growth through intra-regional trade and investment, women engaged in small-scale cross-border trade (SSCBT) face significant challenges that hinder their economic activities and jeopardize their safety. These challenges include limited access to finance, inadequate infrastructure, and cumbersome border procedures, compounded by widespread corruption and gender-based discrimination. These aspects not only hamper their economic activities but also expose them to risks of sexual assault, exploitation, harassment as well as health risks at border crossings. Other major challenges include inefficiency of customs and immigrations procedures and the lack of proper infrastructure and facilities at border crossing points. The project has three components, contributing to the overall objective of providing integrated support to enable safe and prosperous cross-border trade at the Zobué Border Cross Point, thereby promoting gender-inclusive economic growth.

projects.name: Pilot for the Promotion of Integrated Durable Solutions for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Central Mozambique
projects.description: Following the severe impact of Cyclone Idai on the Central Region of Mozambique 2019, resettlement sites were established in view of eventual durable solutions. As per the latest DTM report, currently around 97,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) live across 73 sites in Central Mozambique. However, the conditions for durable solutions as set out in the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) Framework on Durable Solutions for Internally Displaced Persons have not yet been met in most cases – 89% of the IDPs are still living in emergency or temporary shelters.  These combined factors continue to be some of the main drivers of forced migration and vulnerability, as the region remains at risk for weather related shocks as well as the risk of growing grievances and frustrations which are of particular importance as non-state armed groups (NSAG) operate in the country.  Recognizing the importance of improved displacement management, the Government of Mozambique launched a Displacement Management Strategy (PEGDI) in December 2021. IOM proposes an integrated pilot project for Durable Solutions in Buzi District in Sofala Province, based on recommendations from the consultative Durable Solutions report from 2021 and in line with the eight conditions for durable solutions. The project also follows the key recommendations from the UN Secretary General High-Level on Internal Displacement report from 2021, to support the government in piloting the Displacement Strategy.  The project takes a three-pronged approach to improving displacement management: I. IOM will support setting up a SWG for Buzi District and increase members capacities and knowledge on implementing Durable Solutions. This will help coordinate and facilitate Durable Solutions efforts in line with the recommendation of ‘local solutions for local problems’. II. Based on community-identified needs, IOM will support infrastructure and a platform to improve community participation in decision making, including on Durable Solutions in Buzi, specifically for the people living in the resettlement sites in Bopira and Mussimuene. Community engagement and ensuring the people benefitting are part of their Durable Solutions is a key component for sustainability and ownership of solutions. III. To ensure evidence based programming and leveraging on past and ongoing Durable Solutions activities in Central Mozambique, IOM will develop a first progress report against the eight indicators for Durable Solutions as set by the IASC, in resettlement sites in Sofala and Manica. This will provide a baseline and support longitudinal evidence to measure progress toward achieving Durable Solutions and expanding the programming for the Central Region. Through these three coordinated interventions, the project seeks to ensure that displacement management in Mozambique shifts towards an integrated durable solutions approach, taking whole-of-society and evidence-based considerations into account moving forward.

Despite the efforts, access to healthcare, legal protection remains challenging for PWA. To support the Government with implementing the Action Plan, the project “Protection and Promotion of Human Rights of Persons with Albinism in Mozambique: Maputo; Nampula; Zambézia and Tete 2021-2023” was developed. The project is led by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and will be jointly implemented by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and other agencies in partnership with UNESCO. The objective of the project is to reduce attacks, human rights violations, violence, and abduction of persons with albinism nationwide and particularly in those target provinces, particularly in Zambezia, Tete, and Niassa Provinces.

projects.name: IOM Flash Appeal - Flood response in Central and Southern Mozambique
projects.description: Mozambique continues to face various crisis such as climate shocks and conflict. Most recently, heavy rains caused flood and destructions in central and southern Mozambique. Since mid-January 2026, severe flooding has affected more than 724,000 people, prompting the Government to declare a nationwide Red Alert and activate large‑scale evacuation and emergency operations. At the height of the disaster, approximately 100,000 individuals were hosted in around 100 accommodation centres, while hundreds of thousands more remained displaced in host communities and spontaneous sites with extremely limited services.    This project will respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of flood-affected populations, using a multi-sectoral approach. The sectors involved include Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), Protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Health, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). The proposed intervention is in line with the IOM Flash Appeal for the flood response in Central and Southern Mozambique.

projects.description:

(2)	Facilitate access to finance through the development and promotion of new financial services, and the expansion of capitalization opportunities for financial intermediaries;
(3)	Build capacity among informal economy intermediaries and informal enterprises and promote digital finance technology use.
(4)	Foster collective and mutually reinforcing action and innovations to address gaps in selected sectors through the establishment and operationalization of an agricultural commercialization sector collective action platform. This platform will contribute to identifying and addressing systemic gaps in this particular sector of the Mozambican economy.
